political party = a group of people with similar ideas who want to run the country
candidate = a person who wants to be elected
polling station = the place where you go to vote
ballot paper = the paper you mark when you vote
mayor = the person elected to lead a town or city
town hall = the building where local government works
local council = the group that runs local services such as bins and parks
tax = money you pay to the government for public services
news = information about recent events
newspaper = printed pages of news, sold daily or weekly
headline = the title of a news story, in large letters
broadcast = a programme sent out on TV or radio
advert = a picture or film that tries to make you buy something
poster = a large printed picture or notice on a wall
charity shop = a shop that sells used goods to raise money for a good cause
food bank = a place that gives food to people who cannot afford it
old people's home = a place where elderly people live and are looked after
orphan = a child whose parents have died
youth club = a place where teenagers can meet and do activities
scout = a member of a youth group that camps and learns outdoor skills
